5.0.0.en: All the people of God in Jerusalem were led along the way of evil, so they deserved divine punishment; but God in His tenderness wants to pardon them through the intercession of one person who lives by truth and justice, and He asks that such a one be sought, but sadly none was found.

5.0.1.en: God in His love searches for any good work and virtue in you in order to forgive you and support you with His fatherhood, so do not neglect any opportunity to do good, or to pray and be with God, so that you draw out His mercies whatever your sins may be.

5.1.0.en: The evil of the people of God appears in their pretending to have a relationship with Him and to worship Him, such as swearing by His name and not by the pagan gods; but sadly this oath was false. This evil is an example of many evils within them that they try to cover with their outward worship.

5.2.0.en: God looks for truth in the souls of His children, and when He found that they had persisted in evil, He struck them with discipline, whether by words of rebuke or by afflictions, but they were not affected, their hearts were not pained and they did not repent, but they disregarded the word and the discipline as if it were not meant for them.

5.2.1.en: When God allowed them partial destruction, that is, the loss of some of their possessions, or afflictions to come upon them, they murmured, but they did not return to God in repentance.

5.2.2.en: Also their hearts were not affected, and no response to the word of God appeared on their faces, but they hardened their faces and did not submit to Him.

5.3.0.en: The judgment of their God: God's punishment of whoever rejects His commandments.

5.3.1.en: Jeremiah describes them as poor, because of their distance from the knowledge of God; that is, they passed the sentence of destruction on themselves by rejecting God.

5.4.0.en: God commanded Jeremiah to speak to the proud, that is, those who are great in their own eyes, who are the students of the word of God, the opposite of the poor and ignorant; but they became proud of this knowledge and did not use it for repentance, but cast off the commandments of God because they felt them to be a yoke and a heavy bond upon them, and by this they insisted on the way of destruction.

5.5.0.en: In the end, for those who persist in evil there is nothing but to receive the divine punishment through the attack of the armies of Babylon upon them, and he compared it:

5.5.1.en: 1- To a lion that comes from the desert and devours everyone it meets, because of its irresistible strength.

5.5.2.en: 2- To the wolf that goes out in the evening and at night to devour anyone, especially since the wolf devours even if it has been satisfied with its previous prey.

5.5.3.en: 3- To a leopard in its hiding, which may last for several days until it finds the right opportunity and pounces on its prey.

5.5.4.en: All these comparisons show the ferocity of the Babylonian enemy who attacks His people to discipline them because of their many sins.

5.6.0.en: God rebukes Jerusalem and the kingdom of Judah, declaring that He will not pardon the iniquities of her sons, because they trusted in the pagan gods and swore by them, instead of worshiping God and trusting in Him alone. In the same verse He rebukes them because they used His gifts for evil: when He gave them many good things they did not worship Him and thank Him, but rushed into lusts such as bodily adultery, in addition to their worship of idols, which is spiritual adultery. And from the abundance of their evil they were not ashamed of their sin, but shamelessly thronged to the houses of harlots to satisfy their lusts.

5.6.1.en: If you commit any sin, hasten to repentance, and do not try to justify your sins before people, lest you lose your shame and your sense of remorse and persist in sin.

5.7.1.en: Fed: having eaten their food in abundance.

5.7.2.en: Neighed: the sound of the horse; that is, they cried out and rushed to fulfill their lusts.

5.7.3.en: He affirms the same meaning mentioned in the preceding verse by God's comparing His people to animals that have eaten much, so that every male rushes to commit adultery with his neighbor's wife, and these animals are loose, that is, without restraint, because lusts have taken control of them.

5.8.0.en: God asks whether He will not punish for such an appalling evil and avenge Himself on a nation, or a people, that persists in evil?! And the answer, of course, is that He avenges and punishes, and this is what happened in the Babylonian captivity.

5.9.1.en: God commands, through the mouth of His prophet Jeremiah, the armies of Babylon to go up on the walls of Jerusalem and enter the city and destroy it and cut off its branches, that is, every strength she relies on, or fruit that appears in her, because she directed her resources to evil and not to God; but the love of God and His fatherhood appear in His forbidding them to destroy Jerusalem completely, for He intends to discipline her and not to destroy her.

5.9.2.en: When afflictions come upon you, know that they are by God's permission to alert you to repent and return to Him, but in His tenderness He is ready to help you, so that you make up for all that you have missed and return with greater strength than you had before.

5.10.0.en: God judges the idol worship of His people as a betrayal of Him, and it is a grievous sin.

5.11.0.en: The people deceived themselves through the false prophets, expecting that no evil would befall them (expressed as the sword and famine) whatever their sins, and they thought that the mere presence of the temple of God among them in Jerusalem would protect them. By this deception they left God and relied on the pagan gods, because in their eyes they were the true God, and so they exposed themselves to the divine punishment.

5.12.0.en: God judges the false prophets as mere wind, and their words have no value at all; their speech is like the air that cannot be held, and the word of God has no relation to their words.

5.13.0.en: The mighty God, who expresses Himself as the LORD of hosts, declares that He will put powerful words in the mouth of His prophet Jeremiah that will be like a fire that easily burns the wicked people. He compares them to wood, that is, dry stalks of plants. By this He means His punishment of His wicked people.

5.14.0.en: The punishment of God on the kingdom of Judah appears in His allowing Babylon to take vengeance on them, and He describes Babylon as:

5.14.1.en: 1- A nation that comes from afar to take vengeance on them because they rejected their God who was near.

5.14.2.en: 2- Strong in its army, which will shatter the kingdom of Judah.

5.14.3.en: 3- It has an ancient history; it has been strong for a long time and will grow in strength.

5.14.4.en: 4- It has a strange language, so it is impossible to understand it, and it signifies the demons, whose language is evil, foreign to the children of God.

5.15.0.en: Their quiver: the case in which the arrows are placed.

5.15.1.en: He expresses their strength in that their arrows are deadly to the people of God, and they are mighty men who will destroy Jerusalem.

5.16.1.en: He continues the description of Babylon, that it is:

5.16.2.en: 5- Exploitative and fierce, so it eats the food of the people of God sown in the fields, and likewise the animals they raise, in addition to the fruit of the trees, such as the grapes and figs for which the Jews are famous in their land.

5.16.3.en: 6- It will destroy all the fortified cities on which the people of God rely, because they did not trust in Him.

5.17.0.en: God affirms His love and His hope for His people, that He will not destroy them but only discipline them, that perhaps they will repent.

5.18.0.en: When the kingdom of Judah falls into captivity, the people of God murmur, saying: why did God, whom we worship in His temple in Jerusalem, leave us? Ignoring their disobedience to God by the worship of idols in Jerusalem and Judea, so God allowed them to be taken captive to a foreign land whose people worship these gods. For God had cleansed the Promised Land for them and settled them in it to worship Him, but they defiled it with the worship of idols once again, so the land cast them out, and they lost the place with which God had blessed them because of their disobedience to Him.

5.18.1.en: Keep the grace that God has given you, walk in purity, and thank Him for His gifts, and He will continue His grace to you. But if you neglect Him and are occupied with the world and sin, know that all the graces of God that you have can leave you, and if you lose any of them, do not murmur, but repent and return to God, and He will forgive you and restore His grace to you.

5.19.0.en: God rebukes His people who believed in Him and lived with Him, but then returned and lost their spiritual senses and fell into ignorance by their disobedience to God and their worship of idols, so that they no longer saw the truth and understood the will of God.

5.20.0.en: God is astonished at the disobedience of His people and their lack of fear of Him, and He has to remind them through Jeremiah that He is the Controller of all, who sets limits for the sea and for the sandy shores and controls everything in the world; so how is it that His children do not fear Him but worship other gods besides Him to provoke Him?!

5.21.0.en: God also marvels at their persistence in disobedience and their continuing in the worship of idols, forgetting that it is He who gives them their food by the early and the latter rain that waters the plants, so that they eat of them and live; for without Him they would die of hunger.

5.22.0.en: God affirms that the reason for the distress and the captivity into which His people will fall, and which will deprive them of all good things, is their sins and their worship of idols.

5.23.0.en: As he that setteth snares: they crouch at the side of the road, lie in wait and hide, to pounce on people and catch them, that is, seize them, and rob them of their money and take them as their slaves. Snares: traps, or ways to seize people and exploit them and wrong them.

5.23.1.en: He makes clear some of their sins for which God punishes them, which are their cunning, and their hunting of people by hiding in the roads to rob money and to kill, that is, their practice of every act of injustice.

5.24.0.en: He also makes clear that their houses, that is, their hearts and thoughts, are full of evil, so they do not fall into injustice by oversight but with insistence and deliberately. He compares their wicked hearts, which deprive people of their freedom, to a cage in which some birds are shut up and kept from freedom and flight; they enslave others and exploit their abilities, and by this injustice they became rich and held great positions, but they are rejected by God, and He will punish them with captivity.

5.25.0.en: Their strength increased because of their evil, and their strength is expressed by fatness, and their great position by shining, and this drove them to increase in evil and in oppressing the weak, such as orphans and widows, whose rights they robbed; that is, they had outward material success, but their hearts were filled with evil, and deserved divine punishment.

5.26.0.en: God affirms that they deserve severe punishment for their many evils.

5.27.0.en: What will ye do in the end thereof: no one can rescue this people from the wrath that will come upon them in the captivity.

5.27.1.en: He declares that the earth marvels at the evil that happens upon it from His people. The prophets shared in the lie by deceptive prophecies, saying “peace” to the people, and did not rebuke them for their sins that they might repent. The priests joined them and supported them in their false statements, so the people persisted in their evils, supported by their deceiving leaders, and consequently a sad end awaits them, which is punishment by captivity.

5.27.2.en: When an opportunity comes to you to take the right of another, do not think that you gain anything, but you stir up the wrath of God against you. So be faithful in all your dealings, because God sees you and repays you with good or evil according to your works. The sins that caused the destruction of Jerusalem

6.0.0.en: Children of Benjamin: the tribe of Benjamin, which is part of the kingdom of Judah whose capital is Jerusalem. Jeremiah calls them because they represent the inhabitants of Jerusalem and the whole kingdom of Judah.

6.0.1.en: Tekoa: a city about 12 miles south of Jerusalem, and it was the home of the prophet Amos.

6.0.2.en: Beth-haccerem: a city on a hill south of Jerusalem on the road to Bethlehem, which is five miles from Jerusalem.

6.0.3.en: Jeremiah warns the inhabitants of Jerusalem that its destruction by the armies of Babylon has drawn near, and asks those who believe his word to flee from it so that they do not die. He also declares that the destruction will be throughout the land of Judea surrounding Jerusalem, and he chooses from it Tekoa and Beth-haccerem.

6.0.4.en: He also affirms that the attack is fierce like fire that consumes everything it meets, so there will be destruction, that is, a great defeat for the kingdom of Judah.

6.1.0.en: With the eye of a father, God sees the kingdom of Judah as His beautiful and gentle daughter, even though she disobeyed God and persisted in her evil, so He had to discipline her by the Babylonian attack, that perhaps she would repent and return to her spiritual beauty and gentleness.

6.2.0.en: After Jerusalem is destroyed and becomes deserted with no one living in it, the shepherds come to it with their flocks to feed around it and pitch their tents there, so it is no longer a city but merely a wilderness in which sheep graze.

6.3.1.en: God calls the armies of Babylon to wage a mighty war against Jerusalem to discipline her, so they attack her at noon and in the evening and during the night, that is, they attack her at all times until they destroy her; and therefore the inhabitants of Jerusalem groan at the declining of the day, that is, in the evening, because of the attack coming upon them, and likewise at the coming of night, that is, when the shadows of evening lengthen, because they are surprised by a new attack while the war continues.

6.4.0.en: This is a fourth attack, during the night, in which they destroy her greatest dwellings, which are called palaces. The Babylonians attacked Jerusalem at noon, in the evening, at the coming of night, and during the night.

6.4.1.en: When any affliction comes upon you, flee to God by repentance and prayer, and if the affliction increases, do not be distressed, because God who loves you allows it so that you draw near to Him. The affliction does not destroy you, but proves you and makes you grow in the way of the love of God.

6.5.0.en: A mount: walls built around the besieged city, behind which the enemies stand to prevent its inhabitants from escaping.

6.5.1.en: God affirms the ruin and destruction that will come upon Jerusalem, for the Babylonians will destroy the areas surrounding Jerusalem and cut down its trees, and then place them against its walls and set fire to them, so the fire attacks the inhabitants of the city from every side and burns them, and if they try to flee they find that the enemies have set up barricades and stand behind them to kill the inhabitants of Jerusalem and prevent them from escaping. All this divine punishment is because its inhabitants fell into the sin of injustice and did not have mercy on the poor, so God did not have mercy on them and allowed their discipline so that they repent.

6.6.0.en: God declares that the evil of Jerusalem is continual like a spring of water from which water flows constantly, so its inhabitants wrong one another and seize and rob one another, and the weak were afflicted with sicknesses as a result of the injustice of their brothers toward them, and their beating them and assaulting them in various ways.

6.7.0.en: Lest my soul depart from thee: from estrangement, that is, God rejects her and abandons her.

6.7.1.en: God warns Jerusalem that He will abandon her if she rejects discipline and does not repent, and so He will allow her more afflictions, namely the Babylonian devastation and destruction, that perhaps she also will return and repent.

6.7.2.en: Do not wrong another however easy it may be for you, because the just God sees everything, and will punish you for your selfishness and your injustice if you do not return the rights to their owners.

6.8.s.en: (3) The causes of the destruction of Jerusalem

6.8.0.en: They shall throughly glean: after the grapes are gathered they go through the fields to gather any scattered grapes that remain. Vine: a grapevine.

6.8.1.en: God declares that the Babylonians will destroy Jerusalem again and again until she is completely destroyed, as grapes are gathered from the vine again and again until hardly a single grape remains on it, and finally God stops them from doing that. So He says to the grape gatherer, put your hand into the basket in which you gather the grapes and do not pick any other grape, so that a remnant remains for His people to repent and return to Him. The conclusion is that the destruction of Jerusalem will be severe.

6.9.0.en: Their ear is uncircumcised: that is, not circumcised, and it means that their ear is stopped from hearing the voice of God, and their inclination to evil has not been cut off, because circumcision signifies the cutting off of the evil nature and faith in God and sonship to Him.

6.9.1.en: The prophet marvels that he finds no one who hears the word of God, but they stop their ears and neglect His warnings, and more than this they regard the word of God as a reproach, that is, they despise it and reject it, since they rejected the words of Jeremiah and tortured him and threw him into prison because of the word of God with which he warns them, and they regarded obedience to God by submission to Babylon as a reproach, that is, they rejected the divine discipline, so their cities were destroyed and they were killed by the sword.

6.10.0.en: The fury of the LORD: the wrath of God.

6.10.1.en: I am weary with holding in: they exhausted all of God's long-suffering toward them, so His wrath came upon them.

6.10.2.en: Him that is full of days: the aged or the old man.

6.10.3.en: Jeremiah is the voice of God, so he declares that he is full of the divine wrath after the inhabitants of Jerusalem exhausted all their opportunities for repentance, so they deserved death, but God allowed them discipline so that they repent. And He commanded Jeremiah to declare God's pouring out His wrath on all the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the children and the young men and the elders and the aged, because they fell into evil and rejected the commandments of God.

6.11.0.en: Because the people of God wronged one another, He allowed them the Babylonian captivity, which plundered their houses and violated their wives, so the Babylonians were the outstretched hand of God to discipline His people.

6.12.0.en: He showed that the reason for their discipline is their refusal to hear the voice of God (v. 10), and here two other reasons for their discipline appear:

6.12.1.en: 1- Their attachment to the love of money, all of them, both great and small.

6.12.2.en: 2- Their falling into deceit and lying as leaders of the people, who are the priests and the prophets, so the people were led after them.

6.13.1.en: The fourth sin that caused God's discipline of His people is their superficiality and shallowness in treating their problems, so they tried to treat their spiritual diseases and their inner corruption with deceit, as the prophets said to them “Peace, peace” and it will not come upon you, that is, divine discipline; and it would have been better for them to treat their wounds by uncovering them to God by repentance and returning to Him, and He would heal them.

6.14.1.en: The fifth sin that caused discipline for the people of God is persisting in evil, and not being ashamed of their sins and repenting of them, so they deserved discipline and killing and various disciplines.

6.14.2.en: Do not persist in your sins if God alerts you to repent of them, and return to Him, for He is merciful, and He will forgive you every evil and you will return with greater strength.

6.15.s.en: (4) Rejection of the commandments and outward worship

6.15.0.en: God asked His people to review themselves, whether their conduct is sound or mistaken, and asked them to stand at the way of their life to make sure of the soundness of their actions, because they had turned aside in the worship of idols, and He also asked them to look at all their conduct and examine it and ask for the old paths, that is, the books of Moses and the word of God through the prophets, and measure their lives against them, so that if they discover the right way, that is, the commandments of God, they walk in it, and enjoy inner rest and peace from God. But sadly they refused to review themselves so as to walk in the sound ways of the fathers.

6.16.0.en: God appointed the prophets as watchmen over His people, to make them hear His voice like a trumpet warning them so that they return to Him, but they refused.

6.17.0.en: God calls the pagan nations and the peoples of the world as witnesses to the rebellion and disobedience of His people and the sins in which they walk, since their sins exceeded the sins of the nations.

6.18.0.en: He also calls the earth and the people and creatures on it as witnesses to the disobedience of His people, and warns them that He will punish them with disciplines that are the natural result of their evil thoughts and their rejection of the commandments of God.

6.19.0.en: Sheba: a state living in the south-west of the Arabian Peninsula, that is, present-day Yemen.

6.19.1.en: Frankincense: a gummy substance produced from the frankincense plant, which has a sweet smell when burned. Sweet cane: a kind of reed with a sweet smell, and the word “sweet” means a fragrant scent. God declares His displeasure with the offerings and burnt offerings of His people, in which they spend great effort, importing incense materials such as frankincense and sweet cane from distant places like Sheba. This is because this worship is superficial, while their hearts are full of evil, and consequently their worship is worthless, and God rejects it.

6.20.0.en: God decrees that He will punish His people by the Babylonian captivity, in which all will stumble and fall, both the great, such as the fathers, and the small, such as the sons, because they all fell into evil.

6.21.0.en: He describes the discipline as being carried out by the hand of the mighty kingdom of Babylon, which will come from the north-east of the kingdom of Judah, and come from afar, from the farthest known part of the earth at that time, upon His people, and destroy them and take them captive.

6.22.0.en: He continues the description of the strength of Babylon with the following:

6.22.1.en: 1- It uses arrows and the bow to strike the men of Judah from afar and kill them, and spears to kill fiercely and violently whoever it meets.

6.22.2.en: 2- Its attack is violent and its voice is strong like the sea whose waves dash with a roar, that is, the strong sound of the sea.

6.22.3.en: 3- It is organized and possesses many horses ridden by trained horsemen who attack in ranks that sweep through the cities of Israel and kill those in them.

6.23.0.en: When the people hear and see the attack of Babylon, they fall into despair and cannot defend themselves, that is, their hands become slack and fear takes hold of them, and they suffer like a woman in her labor (the travailing one).

6.24.0.en: The people of God will be very afraid, and will hide in their houses, and will not be able to go out into the fields or the roads lest the enemy kill them.

6.24.1.en: May you hold yourself to account every day, to turn back from your sins and repent of your evil thoughts and intentions, so that you can offer holy worship from the heart, which God accepts and rejoices in, and lifts His wrath from you however much your sins deserve punishment.

6.25.0.en: Gird thee: put on a girdle, which is what is worn on the waist and hangs down over the thighs.

6.25.1.en: Sackcloth: coarse garments that signify abasement.

6.25.2.en: Mourning for an only son: weeping over the death of the only son because of attachment to him, and when they lose him they lose all the offspring that would come from him, and so the parents have no offspring.

6.25.3.en: Since the Babylonian army attacked Jerusalem and Judea, God calls her in His fatherhood and calls her His daughter, for He is grieved for her, and calls her to put on sackcloth and wallow in the dust and put it on the head; all these customs they did to show their intense grief and abasement. And He calls her to make a great mourning as for the death of an only son, because of the Babylonians' swooping down on her and destroying her.

6.25.4.en: When an affliction comes upon you, humble yourself before God and weep over your sins, and trust that your tears are precious to Him, for when He sees your repentance He must intervene and deliver you, because His discipline is temporary for your spiritual benefit.

6.26.0.en: God calls Jeremiah and describes him as a tower among the people, where he is a watchman over them and calls them to repent. He also describes him as a fortress, because if anyone repents he will take refuge in him, and he will teach him the commandments of God and by this he escapes the wrath of God.

6.27.0.en: He describes the people as disobedient and rebellious and seeking to cause strife between people and to invent problems, and He describes their unresponsiveness as the hardness of brass and iron, that is, they persist in their evil, insisting on corruption with many sins.

6.28.0.en: The bellows: that which gives air to the fire so that it stays burning strongly in order to melt metals and be rid of their impurities.

6.28.1.en: The lead: it is used to separate the impurities from metals.

6.28.2.en: He compares Jeremiah to the bellows of the metalworker, who blows air to kindle the fire, by proclaiming the voice of God and His warnings so that the people repent, but his work did not bear fruit, and his words went in vain as far as his hearers were concerned, as the lead used for refining the metals is consumed while they have not yet been refined. In the end the bellows itself was burned and the metals do not want to be refined, since they rejected the words of Jeremiah and then killed him by stoning. Thus the refiner did not succeed in his refining of the metals, for the impurities remained in them, that is, the wicked still persist in their evil, rejecting the words of Jeremiah.

6.29.0.en: In the end the divine judgment comes upon His people who persist in evil, and He describes them as reprobate silver. Silver signifies the word of God, that is, the people know the word of God but do not live by it, so God rejected it; and because they rejected God and insisted on that, God also rejected them.

6.29.1.en: God's punishment of His people because of their sins and the worship of idols
